title: Phase-aware KV-slot orchestration and continuous-batch heuristics for heterogeneous long-context variants
creator: Nadia Kapoor
description: Goal: Build and validate a phase-aware KV residency orchestration layer that cooperates with continuous batching to minimize GPU memory pressure for heterogeneous model fleets (Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants) running long-context workloads. This ticket encapsulates design, experiments, and an initial implementation of a lightweight runtime policy that: 1) tracks per-request/variant phase (prompt, steady-state generation, long prefix reuse), 2) adapts KV-slot retention and eviction thresholds per-variant and per-layer, and 3) shapes batch composition to reduce peak working set. The focus is on preventing OOMs on 80GB A100 and improving 95th-percentile tail latency under realistic multi-tenant mixes while preserving model quality and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed by runtime and infra leads with clear heuristics for phase detection and per-variant residency curves
Prototype integrated into the serving runtime as an opt-in policy with feature flag: phase_kv_orchestrator
Bench results: reduce 95th-pctl GPU memory spike by >= 18% on mixed Qwen-13B + Mistral-7B workload with 32k context distribution
No regression in P50 latency beyond 6% and throughput preserved within 10% of baseline for steady-state generation
Automated regression test harness that simulates mixed variant traffic and asserts no OOMs for 1800s with target tail SLOs
Documentation: console toggle, runtime config schema, and a short ops playbook for canary and rollback
comments: 2025-02-20 Nadia Kapoor: Created ticket after spike profiling (see links). Observed correlated tail memory spikes when mixing quantized Qwen variants with Mistral long-context runs. Hypothesis: naive global eviction and single threshold per-GPU fails to account for per-variant cache density and re-use patterns.

2025-02-24 Marcus Lee: Ran initial microbench on dev cluster (a100-80g) with 60/40 Qwen-13B:Mistral-7B steady + prefix reuse mix. Baseline OOMs at 590s for 4 concurrent streams. Captured KV residency histograms and per-layer hotset curves. Uploading artifacts: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4893 and perf dashboard https://dashboard.redwood.ai/runs/phase-kv-1

2025-02-27 Marcus Lee: Prototype policy implemented in rust/mem_orchestrator module. Key ideas: (a) per-variant target_residency vector (layer-wise), (b) phase detector based on request token position and recent prefix-hit ratio, (c) soft-eviction windows with grace periods to avoid thrashing. Initial results: prevented OOMs for 1200s but increased P50 by 4.2% due to more aggressive compaction during spikes.

2025-03-01 Design review notes (Izumi Chen): Prefer exponential decay for residency targets in long-prefix steady state. Raise guardrails for quantized 4-bit variants due to lower eviction cost but higher recompute penalty. Action: add compensation factor for quantized kernels.

2025-03-03 Marcus Lee: Added batch-shaper glue that biases batching toward requests with compatible residency footprints (simple heuristic: group by estimated working set bucket). Observed 12% increase in tokens/sec with smaller 95-pctl memory peaks on stress harness.

2025-03-05 Nadia Kapoor: Preparing canary plan. Need infra approval for dedicated canary pool and feature flag rollout strategy. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4920. Next: synthetic regression suite and longer 3600s soak test on staging.

2025-03-05 Marcus Lee: Noted follow-ups: (1) expose telemetry counters for per-variant eviction rate and average rehydrate cost, (2) run MLOps evals to ensure no generation quality regressions when evictions increase for specific layers, (3) add metric-driven autoscaling hint emission for Dedicated pools.
